title: Night Shift at Magnet Park
summary: Run a theme park’s night rides: flip a magnet to launch or pull down a ring ride, cue a light show, and size a coaster’s magnetic brake.
subject: physics
ncertRef: Section 6.5, Lenz’s law and conservation of energy
concepts: A coil repels an approaching pole, attracts a receding one
No change of flux, no emf
An open loop gets an emf but no current
Work done against the induced current
learningOutcome: The student can use Lenz’s law to find the direction of an induced current and the push or pull it makes, spot when no current flows, and explain a magnetic brake’s heat as work done.

levels.title: Ring Rocket
levels.adds: Baseline: the induced current opposes the change in flux, so a coil repels an approaching magnet and attracts a receding one (Section 6.5).
hints: A pole moving toward the ring raises its flux, so the ring makes the same pole face it and repels it; a pole moving away is attracted.
Field lines leave N and enter S. Seen from above, anticlockwise current makes a field pointing up.
A magnet held still, or a ring with a gap, gives no current at all.

levels.title: The Light Tunnel
levels.adds: New idea: decide if the flux increases, decreases or stays the same, then oppose it (Ex 6.1, 6.2, Examples 6.4, 6.5).
hints: Driving in, springing open or switching the field on raises the flux; driving out, squeezing flat or fading lowers it.
The induced field points against a rise and along a fall.
As you look at the page, anticlockwise current makes a field out of the page (⊙), clockwise into it (⊗).

levels.title: The Brake Run
levels.adds: More steps: the induced current feels a force opposing the motion, and the work done becomes heat (Section 6.5).
hints: The motional emf is Blv, and I = emf/R.
The force on the bar is BIl, against the motion; at a steady speed it equals the pull down the slope.
So B²l²v/R equals the pull: solve for R in ohms, then turn it into milliohms. The power Fv equals I²R.

misconceptions: The induced current helps the change in flux
A strong magnetic field alone induces a current in a loop
A coil attracts an approaching magnet
A loop with a gap carries an induced current
A magnetic brake’s heat does not come from the motion
